html:
The Battle of the Nile was fought from 1 to 3 August 1798 in Aboukir Bay, near Alexandria on the coast of Egypt. A British fleet under Rear Admiral Horatio Nelson destroyed the French fleet that had carried Napoleon's army to Egypt.

Napoleon had sailed in May to seize Egypt and threaten Britain's trade with India. Nelson hunted for him across the Mediterranean for weeks and missed him. The army landed in July and took Cairo. See Napoleon invades Egypt. The French admiral Brueys anchored his 13 big warships in a line close to the shallows and thought he was safe. Nelson found them late on 1 August and attacked at once, with 14. Some of his ships slipped between the French line and the shore, so the leading French ships were fired on from both sides. That night the huge French flagship L'Orient caught fire and blew up. Only two of the 13 French ships of the line escaped. Britain lost none.

The French army was cut off in Egypt, and it surrendered in 1801. The Royal Navy now ruled the Mediterranean. The victory brought Austria, Russia and the Ottoman Empire into a new alliance against France.
